text: {"facts":[{"statement":"The task asks for the minimum total cost of a vertex cover in a tree, with nonnegative vertex costs; for a one-vertex tree, the empty set is valid.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"The input has 1 to 200,000 vertices, costs up to 1,000,000,000, and n−1 undirected edges; output is one integer.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"The one-vertex example has minimum cost 0.","source_ids":["public1"]},{"statement":"The six-vertex example has minimum cost 5.","source_ids":["public2"]}],"open_requirements":["Provide an algorithm and implementation that handle the input limits, including the one-vertex case.","Ensure the result type can represent the maximum possible total cost."] ,"tentative_options":[{"id":"tree_dp","method":"Root the tree and compute, for each vertex, the minimum cost when it is selected and when it is not; combine child states bottom-up.","unverified_assumptions":["The input edges form a connected acyclic tree as specified.","The implementation can process the tree without recursion-depth failure at n = 200,000."]},{"id":"independent_set_complement","method":"Compute the maximum-weight independent set on the tree, then subtract its weight from the sum of all vertex costs to obtain the minimum vertex-cover cost.","unverified_assumptions":["The input edges form a connected acyclic tree as specified.","The implementation uses a sufficiently wide integer type for sums and subtraction."]}],"possible_checks":["Run both public examples and compare with their stated outputs.","Check a one-vertex input with a positive cost returns 0.","Check a tree with a single edge and verify the result is the smaller endpoint cost."]}
